simple.meaning: אָנַף (ʼânaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 14 times in Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, and 2 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 1:37. The surrounding contexts include land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָנַף (H599) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָנַף (ʼânaph) / H599 is traced through Deuteronomy 1:37, Deuteronomy 4:21, Deuteronomy 9:8, Deuteronomy 9:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: Also Yahweh was angry with me for your sakes, saying, “You also shall not go in there.
Furthermore Yahweh was angry with me for your sakes, and swore that I should not go over the Jordan, and that I should not go in to that good land which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance;
Also in Horeb you provoked Yahweh to wrath, and Yahweh was angry with you to destroy you.
Yahweh was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him. I prayed for Aaron also at the same time.

If they sin against you (for there is no man who doesn’t sin), and you are angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near;
Yahweh was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned away from Yahweh, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,
Therefore Yahweh was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight. There was none left but the tribe of Judah only.
“If they sin against you (for there is no man who doesn’t sin), and you are angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captive to a land far off or near;

shall we again break your commandments, and join ourselves with the peoples that do these abominations? Wouldn’t you be angry with us until you had consumed us, so that there would be no remnant, nor any to escape?
Give sincere homage to the Son,‡ or, Kiss the son lest he be angry, and you perish on the way,
You have shown your people hard things.
In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to you, Yahweh; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.

definitions.short: to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged
definitions.full: H599. anaph [ אָנַף אָנֵף, ] verb (breathe, snort) be angry (MI id. , compare Arabic Assyrian etc. in derivatives) **in Hebrew, verb denominative from אַף . — Qal Perfect אָנַפְתָּ Psa 60:3 , etc.; Impefect יֶאֱנַף 2:12 , etc.; — be angry , of ׳י ; usually followed by בְּ 1Kin 8:46 2Chr 6:36 ; Isa 12:1 ; Psa 85:6 ; Ezra 9:14 ; absolute Psa 60:3 ; 79:5 ; compare also 2:12 . Hithpa`el id. always followed by בְּ & always of ׳י , Perfect הִתְאַנַּף Deut 1:37 ; 4:21 ; 9:20 ; Imperfect וַיִּתְאַנַּף 9:8 ; 1Kin 11:9 ; 2Kin 17:18 .
